newsitem.title: MEXICO: Peasant guerrillas kidnap heir to Mexico dynasty.
newsitem.headline: Peasant guerrillas kidnap heir to Mexico dynasty.

text.p: A clandestine group of peasant activists have kidnapped the son of one of Mexico's most controversial political dynasties, newspapers said on Friday, but his father denied that his son was kidnapped.

Mexico's El Universal newspaper said Ruben Figueroa Smutny, 30, was ambushed in a poor neighbourhood of the capital on Wednesday by members of PROCUP, an outlawed radical party believed to have links to Mexico's Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrilla group.
But Ruben Figueroa Alocer, the disgraced former governor of Mexico's impoverished Guerrero state, insisted in a letter to the media on Thursday that his son was vacationing abroad.

Such denials are common in Mexico where families prefer to resolve such incidents without police intervention. But the victim's mother, a family lawyer and a number of friends have confirmed that the kidnapping took place.

PROCUP, banned for espousing methods such as bombing and kidnapping, was part of the guerrilla movement active in Mexico in the 1970s. Many believe it is also working with the EPR, a group of peasant guerrillas active over the past year in Mexico's impoverished Guerrero state.
Newspapers said the kidnappers have demanded the release from prison of three of their comrades and the return of one member of the EPR, missing since late June.

Figueroa Alcocer is head of a dynasty that has long been one of Mexico's most politically influential. He stepped down as governor in 1996 after being widely accused of playing a role in the massacre of 17 peasants in Guerrero in June, 1995.

An attempted cover-up via a video tape fabricated to prove the police were acting in self-defence caused an outcry when national television broadcast the tape that also showed police placing weapons in the dead peasants' hands.
The EPR first appeared on June 28, 1996, the first anniversary of the massacre.

The victim's grandfather, Ruben Figueroa Figueroa, also a one-time Guerrero governor, was kidnapped by a previous generation of guerrillas known as the Party of the Poor. After his release he conducted a dirty war against the rebels in the mountains of Guerrero that faded out after the death of several key rebel leaders.
